comparison.treatment: component_plan quality hypothesis (component_plan_decode_weight=1.0, compiler_decode_mode=tree, grammar_constrained) vs control (compiler_decode_mode=off)

arms.reason: All 3 fixture documents hit the per-document decode timeout (24s) inside the 29s evaluation wall budget; compiler_decode_mode=tree with component_plan_decode_weight=1.0 (grammar-constrained tree decode + generate_max_attempts=3) is substantially more expensive per token than the compiler_decode_mode=off baseline used by cycles 1-4, and this sandboxed CPU host cannot complete even one full grammar-constrained decode inside the shared wall budget at this screening scale.

root_cause: Not a harness code defect. compiler_decode_mode=tree + component_plan_decode_weight=1.0 (grammar-constrained tree decode with generate_max_attempts=3) is a fundamentally more expensive decode path than the compiler_decode_mode=off random-mask baseline every prior cycle in this loop instance used. On this session's CPU-only sandbox host, MAX_RUN_MINUTES=3 caps the whole experiment, leaving only ~29s of evaluation wall budget for n=3 documents against a 24s per-document decode timeout -- not enough headroom for tree-constrained decode to complete even one document. This matches the documented soft-failure class ('ship gates fail on fixture n, null lever deltas, timeouts never stop the loop') rather than a repairable bug: no stack trace, no exception, no incorrect output -- the decode path is simply slower than the available wall budget at this hardware/knob combination.
fix: No code change. This is a knob/scale mismatch (expensive constrained-decode candidate vs a wall-capped CPU fixture screen), not a canonical harness defect. Per continuous.md's self-heal guidance ('change knobs and re-run' when evidence does not name a canonical harness family), the correct response is to not re-select compiler_decode_mode=tree candidates at this wall cap on this host, and to route the next hypothesis toward the driver's own next-ranked priority (grammar_completion_bounds/control-style knobs already proven to complete inside the wall budget) rather than retrying the identical timing-bound arm.

next_priority.hypothesis: Prefer compiler_decode_mode=off (or otherwise wall-budget-compatible) candidates for CPU-sandboxed screening cycles; reserve compiler_decode_mode=tree component-plan comparisons for hosts/wall caps that can complete at least one full grammar-constrained decode.
required_controls: decode_timeout_seconds >= observed CPU tree-decode latency, or
evaluation_wall_seconds budget increased for tree-mode arms, or
compiler_decode_mode=off substituted for the next screening candidate
